open_points.subject: Model M02 — Object creation facts
open_points.text: “the declared characteristics (their list is the specification's and belongs to State 6)” does not say that the characteristics may be absent, while State 0 refuses creation only for “an object without an address” and the preamble says “a fact that may be absent says so”
open_points.question: Must an object’s declared characteristics be supplied when a project is created, or may each characteristic be absent?
options: Every declared characteristic is required at creation
Every declared characteristic is optional
State 1 must declare requiredness separately for each characteristic
open_points.default_guess: Treat every characteristic as optional because State 0 makes only the address required.

open_points.subject: Model M04 — Customer recording facts
open_points.text: “its contact data: name, phone, e-mail, language” does not say which values may be absent, while State 0 refuses recording only for “missing name or kind” and the preamble says “a fact that may be absent says so”
open_points.question: Which contact-data facts must the owner supply when recording a Customer?
options: Name, phone, e-mail and language are all required
Only name and kind are required; phone, e-mail and language may be absent
Requiredness is decided separately for phone, e-mail and language
open_points.default_guess: Require name and kind only, allowing phone, e-mail and language to be absent.

open_points.subject: Imported ArtifactPointer transition times
open_points.text: “A record the import brings in keeps the instants its source holds: ... a pointer's published and superseded instants” omits the withdrawn instant even though M05 says a withdrawn pointer carries “the instant it was withdrawn”
open_points.question: What withdrawal-time fact does an imported pointer with status `withdrawn` carry?
options: The source withdrawal instant is required and preserved
The withdrawal instant may be absent on imported legacy pointers
Registry assigns the import instant as the withdrawal instant
open_points.default_guess: Preserve a source withdrawal instant when available and allow it to be absent for a legacy pointer rather than inventing one.

open_points.subject: Imported ArtifactPointer principals
open_points.text: M05 requires “the instant it was published and by which principal” and, when withdrawn, “the instant it was withdrawn and by which principal”, but the import text says only that pointers and selected instants are kept and never says how imported principals are obtained
open_points.question: What published-by and withdrawn-by facts do imported pointers carry when the legacy source has no ActingPrincipal values?
options: Those principal facts may be absent only for imported legacy pointers
The import owner becomes the recorded principal
The type's owner service is inferred as the publishing or withdrawing principal
The import must supply explicit historical principals
open_points.default_guess: Allow unavailable historical principal facts to be absent on imported legacy pointers and never fabricate provenance.

open_points.subject: Model M09 — AuditEntry identity
open_points.text: AuditEntry is declared an `entity` and “two entries with equal facts are two events”, but its complete facts contain no identifier and the identity section never says who mints or supplies one
open_points.question: What distinguishes and names two AuditEntry entities whose listed facts are identical?
options: Registry mints an opaque AuditEntry id
Registry assigns a monotonic entry ordinal
AuditEntry is a value/event with no separately nameable identity
open_points.default_guess: Have Registry mint an opaque UUID for each AuditEntry.

open_points.subject: Model M09 — AuditEntry subject
open_points.text: The change list says “the import, as one entry whose subject is the migration closure (M10); erasing old entries”, but the subject fact is limited to “the project (`project_id`) or the customer (`customer_ref`) changed ... for a session grant, the session and the project”
open_points.question: What subject facts do the import entry and the audit-entry-erasure entry carry?
options: Generalize the subject to support Project, Customer, AgentSession plus Project, MigrationClosure, and the audit log
Give the import entry a MigrationClosure subject and give the audit-erasure entry no subject beyond its cutoff date
Use a Project or Customer subject for every entry
open_points.default_guess: Use the MigrationClosure as the import subject and no separate model subject for audit erasure, whose cutoff date identifies its target.

open_points.subject: No-op state-change actions and AuditEntry creation
open_points.text: M09 defines an entry as “One significant change of state” and its source as “accepted changes”, but also lists archiving and anonymising as actions that write entries; State 0 says archiving an archived project and anonymising an anonymised project return unchanged, while “Identity formats” says a confirmation id is written into “the audit entry of that action”
open_points.question: Does a successful but state-preserving repeat such as re-archiving or re-anonymising create an AuditEntry and confirmation id?
options: Only an action that actually changes state creates an AuditEntry
Every accepted invocation of a listed action creates an AuditEntry, including unchanged repeats
Every confirmed invocation creates an AuditEntry, while other unchanged repeats do not
open_points.default_guess: Create an AuditEntry only when state actually changes; an unchanged repeat creates no durable confirmation id.
